headline: Low prompt-injection and capability-conflict risk; no documented shared channel or data-flow makes higher-severity pairwise harms unlikely.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-prompts and botpress, and both profiles show empty io_surfaces. Without a bridge such as filesystem, clipboard, or MCP, there is no plausible default prompt-injection path.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future clipboard or MCP bridging between them.
Review any imported prompt content before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles do not show touched data classes, shared storage, or outbound network egress. awesome-prompts is content-writing and botpress is customer-support, but the documented surfaces do not indicate a path for sensitive data to flow from one to the other.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared directory.
Keep both agents on separate local workspaces.
Audit any future integrations for file-reading behavior.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: botpress can install packages, while awesome-prompts has no write or execution surfaces documented. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely, but if both are later pointed at the same mutable workspace, package changes from botpress could interfere with prompt assets from awesome-prompts.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same directory or repository, file-level conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Avoid letting botpress install packages into a shared repo.
Snapshot the workspace before running either agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt repository/list and botpress is a support agent, but no evidence shows botpress automatically treating awesome-prompts output as authoritative. The interaction is therefore only a weak inference, not a documented default cascade.
conditions: IF botpress is wired to consume awesome-prompts output without validation, cascading errors become more likely.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before botpress acts on generated content.
Require schema validation on any handoff payload.
Log and compare source text against downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either awesome-prompts or botpress. With only docs-only profiles and no sensitive data classes, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to score.
conditions: IF either profile later documents regulated data handling or residency constraints, reassess compliance risk.
mitigations: Record data-class handling for both agents.
Add retention and residency notes before deployment.
Re-run the review after any compliance-relevant change.
